## Requirements (contract)

1. Execute all three documented journeys across three dossiers and representative
   tail/unlocated/withheld records in one staged release.
2. Run no-JS, keyboard, print, back/forward, release-citation and
   receipt-to-moderation walkthroughs; distinguish automation, agent walkthrough
   and independent human usability evidence.
3. Record actual user study only if volunteers are explicitly available;
   otherwise provide task protocol and carry the UX evidence gap without
   fabricating satisfaction results.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every eligible selected record is reachable and citable; relationship
      interpretation and unknown-state tasks have evidence-grounded expected
      answers — on the **declared acceptance corpus** (`sig.journey-corpus/1`,
      75 records / 8 partners, tail on browse page 2, unlocated/unreported/
      unresolved/withheld/ghost cases); the committed candidate's record layer is
      honestly `not_applicable` (it publishes 0 records).
- [x] Durable receipt reaches authorized moderation after restart; an approved
      synthetic proposal traverses P32.16a to one canonical disposition and a
      staged public correction, while the receiver cannot directly change facts —
      **executed live on real PG18+PostGIS**, `sig.journey-intake-proof/1`
      10/10 steps ok (`INTAKE_JOURNEY.json`), folded into the portfolio so the
      journey-C checks are `pass`, not `verified_by_test`.
- [x] All material failures receive exact owners/landings and prevent false
      portfolio PASS — enforced structurally (`fail`/`deferred`/`not_applicable`
      refuse to serialize without `owner`+`landing`; an `independent_human`
      check can never serialize `pass`); report keyed to the candidate identity
      digest + the corpus release manifest digest.
- [x] Verification green; meaningful tests for every new behavior; requirement
      ids stamped in PR; DEFERRALS rows + compensating controls; ADR-143;
      closeout protocol followed.

## Plan

Design decision (recorded in ADR-143): **two subjects, one portfolio** —

- The committed P32.23a **candidate** is verified *read-only*: export artifact
  digests, release validation state, identity/ruleset pinning, deferred-evaluation
  disclosure fields, candidate record-surface status, zero-JS, deferral
  dispositions, three-dossier portfolio presence.
- A **declared acceptance corpus** (`sig.journey-corpus/1` export + expectations
  + expected answers) is built by the same `build_release` the candidate used and
  staged into a scratch registry — because the fixture candidate publishes 0
  records, the record-layer journeys run there and the candidate checks are
  `not_applicable` with owner+landing, never silently passed.
- **Journey A** (discover/inspect/trace/search): build validation, record
  reachability, immutable `/r/<pub>` citation, exhaustive browse incl. the tail
  record on page 2, unreported jurisdictions, search (label token, exact entity
  id, `no-public-point` facet, explicit empty result), location states,
  evidence anchors incl. unlocated claims, three dossier pages, static↔JSON
  consistency.
- **Journey B** (relationship/network): typed edges, edge claim resolution,
  bounded navigation, configured_access/observed_use/declared_policy kept
  distinct — candidate network `not_applicable` + `B.eval_deferred` deferred
  (the accessibility/ER-quality disclosure half is test-owned where interactive;
  a real evaluation decision is deferred under `D-R10-HUMAN-1`).
- **Journey C** (correction lifecycle): folded from `sig.journey-intake-proof/1`
  — durable receipt → fresh-connection restart → moderation queue → reviewer
  approval → canonical exactly-once `correct` apply (§16.6 close/revise pair) →
  publish linkage → resolved state, plus live `sig_intake_receiver` write
  refusals on claim/application/moderation.
- **Withdrawals** (`W.*`): entity-level withhold denies entity routes,
  claim-level withhold denies all asserting records, current registry applies to
  historical namespaces, `sig.tombstone/1` content-free JSON tombstone,
  unaffected routes permitted.
- **Walkthroughs** (`WT.*`): evidence classes separate — `agent_walkthrough`
  for no-JS/print/release-citation (agent-executed, never described as user
  sessions), `verified_by_test` for keyboard/back-forward/receipt-traversal
  (web e2e owns the interactive proof).
- **`UX.independent_sessions`** — `independent_human`+`deferred`; protocol
  landed, gap carried honestly.
- **CLI** — additive `sig-ops journey-verify` (portfolio + JSON/Markdown emit +
  one-line status) and `sig-ops journey-intake` (DSN-gated proof executor; a
  missing proof degrades journey C to `verified_by_test` citing
  `tests/db/test_journey_portfolio_pg.py`, never to `pass`).

## Deviations / honest notes

- The fixture candidate publishes **0 records / 0 edges** — record and
  relationship journey semantics are `not_applicable` on it and ran on the
  declared `sig.journey-corpus/1` acceptance corpus instead (synthetic,
  never-published; regenerated by `journey_verify` deterministically). The
  report states this in the first paragraph — never a hidden substitution.
- `WT.keyboard`/`WT.back_forward`/`WT.receipt_to_moderation` are
  `verified_by_test` (web e2e owns the interactive/browser proof) — labelled,
  not promoted to agent or human evidence.
- `B.eval_deferred` stays `deferred` — the measured evaluation decision is the
  deferred S3 spine (`D-R10-HUMAN-1`); the portfolio discloses, never simulates.
- `UX.independent_sessions` `deferred` — no volunteers; protocol landed;
  `D-R10-USERS-1` OPEN.
- No live exposure, no `activate()`/`rollback()` on the candidate, no intake
  receiver operation — `D-R10-PUBLISH-1`, `D-R10-LIVE-1`, `D-P32.16-1` OPEN.
